result.question: How does Nvidia describe competition for its data center products?
result.answer: NVIDIA describes competition for its data center products as intense and potentially intensifying, with companies competing on price, total cost of ownership, and performance, which has resulted and may in the future result in lower-than-expected selling prices or demand for its products [c1]. Some competitors operate their own fabrication facilities and have longer operating histories, larger customer bases, more comprehensive IP portfolios and patent protections, more design wins, and greater financial, sales, marketing and distribution resources than NVIDIA [c1]. These competitors may acquire market share, more effectively identify and capitalize on opportunities in new markets, more quickly transition their products, and impinge on NVIDIA's ability to procure sufficient foundry capacity and scarce input materials during supply-constrained environments [c1]. Additionally, some of NVIDIA's customers are developing their own ASICs and other products, including designs optimized for certain workloads that may not require all the features and functionality NVIDIA's data center systems provide [c1]. Others may offer cloud-based services that compete with NVIDIA's AI cloud service offerings, and NVIDIA may not be able to establish market share sufficient to achieve the scale necessary to meet its business objectives [c1]. If NVIDIA is unable to successfully compete in this environment, demand for its products, services, and technologies could decrease, which may negatively impact its business [c1].
